summary: Andrew Olendzki works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Lancaster University and under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served as executive director at the Insight Meditation Society, Barre Center for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003–2014), and senior scholar at Mind and Life Institute (attested 2014).

Andrew P. Tuck is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Princeton University and was taught by Victor Preller, Jeffrey Stout, William E. Kennick, Robert A. F. Thurman, John Pemberton, D. Dennis Hudson, Daniel H. H. Ingalls, Alan Sponberg, and Richard Rorty.

Andrew Quintman is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Jay L. Garfield and served as an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University (attested 2015).

Andrew Sihler is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard University (~1958–1962) and Yale University (~1962–1967) under Warren Cowgill (~1964–1967). He held a post at the University of Wisconsin–Madison from ~1967 to 1998.

Andrew Watsky is a specialist in Japanology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Oberlin College (~1975–1979) and Princeton University (~1986–1994). He held a post at Vassar College from ~1994 to 2008.

Andrew William Kennedy works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Leeds (attested 2006), where he studied under doctoral supervisors Philip A. Mellor and Kim Knott.

Andrey Klebanov is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his MA (-2010) and PhD (-2016) at the University of Hamburg, studying under Harunaga Isaacson, among others. He was appointed professor at Kyoto University (attested 2019).

Andrey Terentyev is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Faculty of Philosophy at Saint Petersburg State University (~1970–1975) and worked at the Museum of the History of Religion from ~1977 to 1998.

Andrzej Gawroński was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv (1902–1906) and Leipzig University (~1903–1906). He held posts at Jagiellonian University (1916–1917) and the University of Lviv (1917), and founded the Polish Oriental Society and Polish Linguistic Society.

András Róna-Tas is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1950–1955) under Gyula Ortutay and Lajos Ligeti. His main academic posts included Eötvös Loránd University (1956) and the University of Szeged (1968–2002).

André Bareau was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Sorbonne, EPHE, and Collège de France under Jean Filliozat and Paul Demiéville. He held posts at the CNRS (1947–1951), EPHE (1956–1973), and Collège de France (1971–1991).

André Caquot was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure (~1943–1947) and EPHE (~1947–1951), he held posts at the EPHE (~1955–1972), University of Strasbourg (1957–1960), University of Paris (1964–1968), and Collège de France (1972–1994).

André Couture is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. He studied at Laval University (~1965–1971), EPHE (~1971–1977), and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1971–1977). He held an academic post at Laval University starting around ~1979.

André Godard was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux-Arts (~1900–1909) and held a post at the University of Tehran from ~1934 to 1953.

André Martinet was a linguist who studied at the Sorbonne (~1926–1937) and under Antoine Meillet (~1930–1936). He held academic posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1938–1947), Columbia University (~1947–1955), and the University of Paris (~1955–1977).
André Mazon was a linguist. He studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1900–1904) and Charles University (~1904–1905), and served as a professor at the Collège de France from 1923 to 1951.

André Padoux was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at the University of Paris. Supervised by Louis Renou and Olivier Lacombe, he was director of the Institut Français de Francfort (~1959–1964) and a researcher and research director at the CNRS (1959, 1982).

André Wedemeyer was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and linguistics. He completed his doctoral studies under August Conrady (~1906–1910) and held an academic post at Leipzig University from ~1914 to 1945.

Andy Rotman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the University of Chicago under supervisors Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins, and held a post at Smith College (attested 2013–2017).

Angela Falco Howard is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She completed her doctorate at New York University under Alexander C. Soper and Yoshito S. Hakeda, and served as a professor at Rutgers University (attested 2005).
